text: It was two-forty in the morning. In the basement, the sour smell of the rye fermenting really overpowered the bleach and the floor. Arthur wiped his hands on his jeans. He went and rummaged behind the wicker bannetons, on the wire rack down low, the library had a copy of The Count of Monte Cristo, it was taped up. Fourth Thursday. Same as the others, the spine lined up with the steel edge. He pulled it out. Stuck to the cover was a square of blue prescription pad paper, and it said in ballpoint, the ink had gone through: the baker in chapter five reminds me of you, thank you for keeping the lights on. Arthur traced with his thumb the deep indentation the pen had left. The only sound was the compressor shuddering. Out of the back of the book fell a due date card, yellowed, red ink, stamped three days overdue. He went to the prep table, took a warm cinnamon roll, it had glaze spots, wrapped it in parchment paper, put it in his coat pocket with the book.
